Full summary: Adversarial review round 1: three confirmed defects in the D1-D5 fixes, all fixed — archive_stale now tombstones dismissed blackboard entries and states honestly that unarchive restores decisions only; auto-archive trigger and fired sweep share NO_AGE_CUTOFF (clock-skew #35 variant closed); twining_status needs_archiving computed from the archive partition instead of the raw count
Decisions: Chose to tombstone archive_stale's blackboard dismissals and correct the tool text rather than extend twining_unarchive to restore blackboard entries — restoring from tombstones needs an id-collision-safe re-append path that deserves its own design; honest text plus a full-content tombstone removes the data-loss-behind-a-recoverability-promise today; Chose to pass NO_AGE_CUTOFF to the trigger-fired sweep so trigger and sweep have literally identical partition inputs — future-stamped entries (git-synced fast-clock stores, VM clock resets) were counted but never archived, re-firing a no-op sweep on every post; the verifier reproduced this executable before the fix
Findings: warning: 4 of 5 review finder dimensions stalled (machine contention window, 6 retries each) — only the d4 lens ran; resuming the workflow for d2-lifecycle, d5-cursor, d3-staleness, and cross-cutting coverage before release; The workflow script had a post-processing bug: results.filter(Boolean) before flatMap((r,i)=>DIMENSIONS[i]) mislabels dims when finders fail — the two confirmed findings labeled d2-lifecycle actually came from the d4-partition finder
